text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 0.89% today, continuing a strong two-week rally of 8.91%. The move reflects tightening global oil supplies: Saudi Arabia shut down a critical pipeline bypass today after Iranian attacks, pushing Brent crude above $108 per barrel, while U.S. refineries are running at 97.8% capacity—near maximum—and diesel prices just hit record highs above $6 a gallon. For a refiner like this, higher crude prices and constrained fuel supplies mean stronger profit margins on the fuel they produce and sell.

The escalating Middle East conflict—Iran downing a U.S. drone over the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi pipeline damage—has created sustained upward pressure on oil markets, with the gap between U.S. crude ($97.26) and global Brent ($109.51) widening. This geopolitical risk premium, combined with U.S. diesel scarcity driving record prices, has positioned refiners favorably for the near term, even as inflation concerns persist globally.
